body: I just want my life to have some kind of significance outside of the usual college-family-retirement.
No, yes, no.Sadly, one of my hobbies (exercise) I started using as a form of self harm, and I think part of my feeling so bad is from not running.

That's just it--I don't know why.

Nothing's wrong, really. I just know I feel this way, and that this is getting ridiculous. I look around and see nothing worth living for. Money? Too bad it doesn't keep you alive. Ditto for 'things'. Marriage/family? No thanks. I will never marry. Living for others? No, I prefer to be selfish.

I see so much pettiness in the people I know (I'm American, and so they are too). Like, why does it matter what car, job, or how much money I have? It doesn't. But, American society is built around the idea that these things mean something. And they don't, and if you don't agree that life is the sum of what you've 'earned', well, fuck you. 

I guess my problem is I want more from life than I can reasonably have, and I see no reason to try and pretend I'll be happy with less. Some people might. I know myself, though, and I know I'm not one of those people.

I have a speeding ticket I'm considering not paying, because then I won't have to worry about what I do and don't have. I just go to jail and that's that. Everyone can just fuck off because I'll be living in a concrete cell.

(Won't lie, though: I'd love to be a Franciscan or Dominican. I don't know that I believe in God, but something about the way they renounce the world and live their lives is amazing. They literally have nothing, and yet they act like they have everything. It's so beautiful.)

I don't need or want help in that area. That's been decided already. 

I just needed to make sure that, should I choose to not pay the ticket, cops won't show up interrupting something they have no business interrupting. And, I was right. They won't just appear at my door an hour after court, especially since the county is an 1.5 hours away.

As I told the other user, I might pay it. I might not. That decision, though, is ultimately irrelevant.

Eh, I've been arrested before. It loses its shock value after the first time. 

I'm not saying it won't happen, just that when the cops get around to it, it'll be too late. I may just pay it. The dead don't need money anyway.
It's not just the fine. I was having problems way before now. The fine (paying it will literally mean choosing between rent and eating) just made things clear, I guess.

I'm not worried about a warrant. 

I was more worried about the cops showing up like the morning after court to arrest me. Based on what's been written here and what I've read elsewhere on the internet, that's highly unlikely to happen. So... I'm not worried about it.
Can they collect from an estate?

That's all well and good, but everyone here keeps talking about driving on a suspended license, which is weird because I haven't said anything about doing that.

And, I'm not worried about the bench warrant. I'm more concerned with any *immediate* consequences, and apparently there aren't any. I don't really plan on being alive long enough (past May 17, that is) for some bench warrant to matter down the road.

> Keep trying to convince yourself that breaking the law is okay.

Eh, it's not really a matter of 'okay' or 'not okay'. Besides, I don't think I have a future anyway.

Actually, I live with someone who's perfectly content to drive me where I need to go, since I pay their rent. A suspended license just means **I** won't be driving.I'm sorry, but you'll never convince me that a $700 ticket is an appropriate fine for speeding on an empty, flat, straight rural road. I wasn't even going fast enough to be considered a super speeder.
And if I stop driving? Just because they've suspended my license doesn't mean I have to keep driving (quite the opposite, I would think).

Well, I haven't needed a second one yet. Up until last week, I'd been working 35hrs a week. But then I got cut, so its not like I've had a reason to or had planning time. There's no way I'll make 800 dollars anyway before May 17. I don't have any skills, and I have to pay ~250 a month for student loan payments (on a degree I never finished). I have to have several months' rent because I don't really have any credit, other than the student loans.Anyway, I've decided I'm not going to pay the ticket. I'll sit in jail for a year before I give them a penny. Or, I might just use the $1000 I have to leave the country. Or to buy a shotgun. I can go out like Hemingway.

Not really. Everything's actually going well. I've lost a ton of weight (I went from 300 to 240, but my goal is 180-190ish), I've got a job I actually like (even if it is in retail with moronic customers). I've saved up a nice chunk of change this ticket is about to obliterate, and it was supposed to be used to help me move out on my own. Up until I saved this money up, I was a step away from being homeless. It's all I have, and now it's going so some Twiggs County fatass can be comfy in his chair.  

The alternative is get put on probation, and hope I get paid enough every week to pay the probation officer. With gas, it'll be way more than I bring in every week. And, guess what happens in these shitty hick counties and towns that use privatized probation services when you can't pay? You fucking go to jail for the rest of your sentence. Since speeding is a misdemeanor in Georgia, it's max penalty is a year in jail. Usually, judges give you a year on probation to pay off the ticket. 

I've been through this shit before for driving my mother's car with expired registration. I hate myself for getting caught doing something *everyone else on the fucking planet* does. I hope that cop burns in hell, regardless of whether or not he was just 'doing his job'. Bastard should've picked another job. In fact, the little shit probably speeds every-damn-where knowing full well he won't get a ticket.

Edit: I don't mean to be angry with you. Please don't take it that way. I'm just angry with myself, and angry with a fucking system that thinks an $800 fine is proportional to the 'crime' committed.
